 The deadline for paying non-agricultural land tax is approaching; people should take note to avoid penalties.
 (Dan Tri Newspaper) - Today (November 2nd) is the deadline for paying non-agricultural land use tax for the year. People are going to bank branches to complete the procedures, avoiding late payment penalties starting tomorrow.
 Báo Dân trí • 02/11/2026 Follow Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e Add Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e 0 According to Decree 252/2026, for the first payment of non- agricultural land use tax, taxpayers have 30 days from the date the tax authority issues the notice to fulfill their obligation. From the second year onwards, non-agricultural land use tax is paid once a year, no later than October 31st.
 This year, because October 31st falls on a Saturday, the tax filing deadline has been moved to the next working day, which is today (November 2nd).
 With the land tax payment deadline approaching, people are flocking to banks to complete the procedures. 
 Previously, information on tax forums indicated that some residents had reported receiving notices from the tax authorities despite having paid non-agricultural land use tax. In other cases, individuals had transferred ownership of their apartments but still received tax notices; while some residents had lived in the apartment building for many years without ever declaring or paying taxes and without receiving any notices…
 Currently, the two most common ways to pay non-agricultural land tax are through the eTax Mobile application or through the Agricultural and Rural Development Bank ( Agribank ) for collection.
 To pay their taxes and avoid tax arrears and late payment penalties, many people choose to go directly to Agribank branches. At some branches in Hanoi , during peak times, the number of people coming to transact increases, concentrating at the tax information and collection counters. Bank staff assist in looking up information, determining the amount due, and completing the payment procedures.
 An employee at an Agribank branch on Trung Hoa Street (Hanoi) said that customers only need to notify the bank and the collection process will be completed immediately without requiring any declaration. Otherwise, customers will be guided to fill out the form before payment. 
 Tax payment notice.
 An employee at the Agribank branch on Trung Kinh Street (Hanoi) said that in order for the bank to collect non-agricultural land use tax, customers need to present the tax payment notice issued by the tax authority. This serves as the basis for bank staff to look up information, determine the amount to be paid, and complete the transaction.
 According to this employee, most people who come to transact business bring tax notices, while some need staff assistance in double-checking information and guiding them through the payment process.
 Bank staff also reminded customers that November 2nd is the deadline for paying non-agricultural land use tax for the regular payment period of the year. If payment is made after this deadline, individuals may be subject to late payment penalties as stipulated, calculated on the outstanding tax amount and the number of days overdue.
 According to the 2025 Tax Administration Law, the late payment penalty is 0.03% per day on the outstanding tax amount. Therefore, if taxes are not paid on time, starting from November 3rd, people will begin incurring late payment penalties.
 You may also like Late payment penalty = Amount of tax owed × 0.03% × number of days of late payment.
 For example, with a tax arrears of 500,000 VND, if the taxpayer is 10 days late in payment, the late payment penalty is calculated as 500,000 VND × 0.03% × 10 days, equivalent to 1,500 VND. If the delay is 30 days, the late payment penalty is 4,500 VND; if the delay is 60 days, it is 9,000 VND. 
 Cash transaction at an Agribank branch (Photo: Tien Tuan).
 Tax authorities review over 3.3 million land tax returns. 
 Regarding information related to the management of non-agricultural land use tax, the Tax Department stated that it has issued numerous directives and guidelines to provincial and city tax authorities on tax management, with a focus on reviewing and standardizing data on the industry's application systems. The tax authorities have completed the review of 95.57% of the total of over 3.372 million tax declarations requiring review.
 Along with promoting data standardization, the Tax Department has advised the Ministry of Finance to report to the Government on reducing administrative procedures and document requirements in the tax sector. New regulations aim to reduce the need to resubmit information and documents that the state agency already possesses and is eligible for data connection; and to eliminate the requirement for taxpayers to resubmit tax returns in cases where the tax authority has already connected and has complete land information from the national database and the database of the state land management agency.
 However, based on the actual situation, in some areas, taxpayer information and land plot information are still not fully updated, leading to inaccurate notifications of non-agricultural land use tax obligations.
 In some areas, the process of receiving and handling taxpayer feedback and suggestions electronically has not been timely; in some cases, the responses have been unclear and have not definitively resolved the issues. Coordination, data verification, and the assignment of responsibilities for handling these matters also need further improvement. 
 Me Tri Thuong Ward viewed from above (Photo: Nguyen Hai).
 Based on that, the Tax Department reviewed the implementation situation in localities, assessing the difficulties in the process of managing non-agricultural land use tax, from data updating and tax liability determination to receiving and processing taxpayer feedback.
 The Tax Department continues to require units to review the progress of assigned tasks, proactively prepare reports and documents, and propose solutions to address difficulties and obstacles within their areas of responsibility. The focus is on improving the quality of tax management data, ensuring accurate determination and notification of tax obligations, and promptly addressing feedback and suggestions from taxpayers.
 This applies to cases where taxpayers have already paid but still receive a notice stating that the amount payable is 0 VND. 
 You may also like Hanoi Tax Department announced that, starting in 2025, the tax authorities will collect non-agricultural land use tax via eTax Mobile and other cashless payment methods. If taxpayers have already paid, the amount due will be displayed as 0 VND at the time the notification is issued.
 However, the tax authorities still send tax payment notices to taxpayers to show that the tax management system has recorded the amount of tax paid by the taxpayer and to allow taxpayers to manage information on the land plots for which taxes have been declared and paid.
 In cases where land use rights have been transferred, bought, sold, or gifted but non-agricultural land use tax still remains due , taxpayers need to check the time period for which the payment was made; review whether the transfer information and the transferee's details have been updated. Simultaneously, prepare the contract, documents confirming the transfer of rights, the linked file code (if any), and proof of payment; and submit a request for verification to the tax authority where the property is located. The tax authority will cross-check and coordinate with the land authority to make adjustments when necessary.
 Regarding cases of apartment owners who have not declared or paid non-agricultural land use tax and have never received a tax payment notice , the Hanoi City Tax Department suggests that the reason may be due to non-declaration or a change of ownership that has not been updated. Taxpayers should prepare contracts and documents confirming the transfer of ownership, and the linked file code if available; and contact the tax authority where the apartment is located. The tax authority will cross-check and coordinate with the land authority to make adjustments when necessary.
 Hanoi City Tax Department advises apartment owners to carefully check information regarding the land area allocated to the apartment. When transferring ownership of an apartment, taxpayer information needs to be updated promptly to avoid errors in determining tax obligations.
 Taxpayers can look up their tax obligations, receive notifications, and pay taxes directly on the Etax Mobile app.
